questions.stem_markdown: A registrar has established rapport with a 16-year-old during an adolescent review in a Sydney clinic and is about to move from the presenting complaint into more sensitive psychosocial screening. According to the notes, what is the **best next step** in structuring the consultation?

options.text: Start a detailed substance-use screen immediately before setting any expectations about the conversation
Ask the parent to answer the psychosocial questions first so the adolescent only needs to confirm the history
Discuss confidentiality and explain that the review will now move into broader psychosocial questions
Skip psychosocial screening unless the adolescent independently raises a sensitive concern
Move straight to sexuality questions first because the most sensitive topic should be asked before anything else

questions.explanation_markdown: The notes describe comprehensive adolescent assessment as beginning with **engagement and discussion of confidentiality** before broader psychosocial assessment. They also list the HEEADSS domains that structure this screening. That makes it best to set expectations and discuss confidentiality before moving into sensitive psychosocial topics.

why_others_wrong.A: The source material places discussion of confidentiality before detailed psychosocial or substance-use assessment.
why_others_wrong.B: The notes support direct adolescent assessment rather than making the parent the primary source for the psychosocial screen.
why_others_wrong.D: The source material presents psychosocial assessment as a structured part of adolescent care, not something to omit unless volunteered.
why_others_wrong.E: The notes do not support jumping straight to sexuality ahead of the broader structured assessment.

key_takeaways: After rapport is established, the next step is to discuss confidentiality before sensitive screening.
Adolescent psychosocial assessment is structured rather than ad hoc.
Clear consultation structure supports better adolescent engagement.
